rows: 117 · Roman Empire Reaches Its Greatest Extent — The empire's extent peaked in 116–117; Trajan died in August 117 and Hadrian withdrew from Mesopotamia soon after.
180 · Death of Marcus Aurelius — Died 17 March 180, at Vindobona (Vienna) or Sirmium; sources differ. AT chosen for Vindobona.
235 · Severus Alexander Murdered by His Own Troops — Killed in March 235 near Mogontiacum (Mainz). Name avoids 'Crisis of the Third Century' because it names the century.
284 · Diocletian Becomes Roman Emperor — Proclaimed at Nicomedia (Izmit, Turkey) in November 284. The tetrarchy itself dates from 293; the description doesn't tie it to the accession year.
1326 · Ottomans Capture Bursa — Bursa (Byzantine Prusa) fell in April 1326 after a siege of several years.
1517 · Ottomans Conquer Mamluk Egypt — Ridaniya was fought in January 1517; Syria fell after Marj Dabiq (August 1516).
1520 · Suleiman the Magnificent Becomes Sultan — Acceded September 1520; died 1566 at the siege of Szigetvár.
1683 · Ottoman Siege of Vienna Fails — The siege began in July; the relief battle was fought on 12 September 1683.
1699 · Treaty of Karlowitz Signed — Signed 26 January 1699 at Sremski Karlovci.

1789 · Selim III Becomes Sultan — Acceded April 1789; the New Order army dates from 1792–93; deposed 1807, killed 1808. The phase boundary is his accession (the source document's 1792 would be the army, not the reign).
1839 · Edict of Gülhane Launches the Tanzimat Reforms — Proclaimed 3 November 1839.
1914 · Ottoman Empire Enters World War I — Black Sea raid 29 October 1914; Russia, Britain and France declared war in early November.
